annotation.material_differences: Response A explicitly deprioritizes understanding the customer’s explanation and says not to spend long digging into it, while B and C at least frame the issue as a confirmation/booking mismatch and retain some willingness to check the latest record. This can affect CSS01-C1 and CSS01-C3 because A is less focused on clarifying the actual problem before selecting a resolution. C also adds an assumption that the customer is probably just seeing an old message, which is a stronger factual presumption than B’s wording and could change issue framing.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: All three responses share a general tendency to check the booking record and reissue or restore confirmation, but they do not preserve the same decision-relevant evidence for problem identification. A more clearly skips customer clarification and assumes the system error is the main issue, whereas B and C at least acknowledge a confirmation mismatch and starting from the latest booking record. Because the question asks how to establish the customer’s actual problem before helping, A’s lower emphasis on clarification is a material difference under the issue-definition criteria.
